subject: Approval request: Dedicated Burst option pricing bands + margin guardrails (GA target June)
body:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 19, 2025 at 5:12 PM PST
Subject: Approval request: Dedicated Burst option pricing bands + margin guardrails (GA target June)
Attachments: Burst_UnitEconomics_Sensitivity_v4.xlsx; Dedicated_Burst_Packaging_Pricing_Bands_2025-02-19.pdf

Hi Laura,

Requesting Finance approval on proposed pricing bands + required margin guardrails for the Dedicated “Burst Capacity” option (shared Redwood-managed burst pools; GA target June).

TL;DR
- Customers on Dedicated can temporarily exceed their baseline reserved GPUs by borrowing from burst pools (within region/hardware class).
- Burst will be metered separately as “Burst GPU-hours” (internally derived from GPU-seconds; exported to billing pipeline).
- Positioning: predictable baseline + paid bursts for known peaks; no requirement to permanently upsize reservation.

Proposed pricing bands (GA)
We’d like to publish bands (not a single number) to allow sales to anchor and keep us within approved floors:

H100 (us-east/us-west): $9.50–$12.50 per Burst GPU-hour
- Recommended list: $11.00

L40S (us-east/eu-west): $2.75–$3.75 per Burst GPU-hour
- Recommended list: $3.25

A10-class (legacy regions only): $1.60–$2.25 per Burst GPU-hour
- Recommended list: $1.90

Assumptions behind the above (high level)
- We’re not changing baseline Dedicated reservation pricing in this thread.
- Burst is “best effort availability” (not reserved), with strict admission control/fleet safety caps.
- We expect burst usage to cluster into short windows (batch/indexing jobs, launches, weekly peaks), not constant 24/7.

Unit economics summary (from the attached sensitivity model)
- Under expected burst utilization (p50: 10–20% of baseline hours), the recommended list pricing yields ~58–64% gross margin on burst units (after infra overhead), with worst-case stress (p90 utilization + higher denial handling + elevated support) still above 50%.
- Key drivers: H100 spot volatility (if we’re forced into expensive supply), and tail-latency guardrails causing effective throughput degradation (more “paid time” per token).

Requested approvals
1) Approve the above price bands (with a floor we cannot go below without Finance sign-off).
2) Approve packaging guardrails we plan to hard-code into contracts/SLAs:
   - Burst is non-guaranteed and may be denied due to pool saturation / fleet safety caps.
   - Baseline Dedicated SLAs remain unchanged; burst units are excluded from latency SLO commitments.
3) Confirm required billing accuracy gates (e.g., reconciliation thresholds) before GA.

If it’s helpful, I can grab 20 mins Thursday/Friday to walk through the model.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Product, Dedicated
Redwood Inference


From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 20, 2025 at 9:06 AM PST
Subject: Re: Approval request: Dedicated Burst option pricing bands + margin guardrails (GA target June)

Lauren,

Thanks—went through the PDF and skimmed the sensitivity workbook. A few questions before I approve bands:

1) What’s the implied floor GM at the *lowest* band for H100 ($9.50) under a “bad but plausible” scenario (higher COGS + more admission denials + telemetry lag causing inefficiency)?

2) Are we assuming any “burst-on-burst” overhead (support load, SRE incidents, customer comms) in the model, or is it purely infra COGS?

3) Contract language: I agree burst must be best-effort. Please ensure Sales can’t imply burst availability is reserved or guaranteed.
   - We should be explicit that baseline is the reserved capacity; burst is opportunistic.

4) Billing: I want a concrete GA gate: what reconciliation threshold (e.g., <0.5% variance) and what happens when we detect over/under-counting. Also confirm we have idempotency on retries.

If you can answer those (even briefly), I’m comfortable approving with conditions.

Laura Bennett
Finance
Redwood Inference


From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 20, 2025 at 1:41 PM PST
Subject: Re: Approval request: Dedicated Burst option pricing bands + margin guardrails (GA target June)

Laura,

Answers inline:

1) Floor GM at H100 $9.50 under stress
- Using the “H100 high COGS + low effective throughput” scenario tab (worst case we modeled), $9.50 still lands ~49–51% GM on burst units.
- The two assumptions that push it down are (a) procurement/region premium and (b) “effective throughput penalty” from guardrails (i.e., more time for the same output).
- If we see both of those conditions persisting in a region, we’d plan to either (i) constrain burst caps, or (ii) push customers to $11+ pricing for that hardware/region.

2) Support/SRE overhead
- Workbook includes a conservative overhead factor (line item “Ops overhead / incident reserve”) applied as a % of burst revenue.
- It does not attempt to predict black-swan incidents; we’re relying on guardrails + SLO gates to reduce likelihood, and we’ll review after beta.

3) Contract / Sales messaging
- Agree. Packaging doc already states “best effort” and explicitly excludes burst from any latency guarantee.
- We’re aligning with Legal separately, but will make sure enablement says: baseline = reserved, burst = opportunistic + metered.

4) Billing GA gates
- Proposed gates (happy to adjust):
  a) Reconciliation variance: <= 0.5% monthly between raw metering export and billing pipeline aggregated line item, per tenant.
  b) Idempotency: require idempotency keys on retry paths before GA (ENG ticket already tracked; if not complete, we hold GA in that region).
  c) Remediation: if we detect over-counting, issue credit in same billing cycle; if under-counting, we do not “claw back” retroactively without explicit customer notice (we’ll treat as a Redwood issue and fix forward).

If you’d like, I can update the pricing bands doc to explicitly call out (1) floor GM assumptions, and (2) reconciliation gates as GA blockers.

Lauren


From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 21, 2025 at 8:22 AM PST
Subject: Re: Approval request: Dedicated Burst option pricing bands + margin guardrails (GA target June)

Approved with conditions.

Finance approval scope
- Approved the GA pricing bands as proposed:
  - H100: $9.50–$12.50 per Burst GPU-hour (floor = $9.50)
  - L40S: $2.75–$3.75 per Burst GPU-hour (floor = $2.75)
  - A10-class: $1.60–$2.25 per Burst GPU-hour (floor = $1.60)

Conditions / guardrails (must be true for GA; otherwise re-approval required)
1) Contract + enablement must clearly state:
   - Burst is best-effort, non-reserved, and may be denied.
   - Baseline Dedicated reservation is the only reserved capacity.
   - Burst usage is excluded from latency/throughput SLA commitments (baseline SLAs unchanged).

2) Billing/metering gates
   - Reconciliation variance <= 0.5% per tenant per month (metering export vs invoiced burst line item).
   - Idempotency on retries required (no double-counting on retried requests).
   - Documented remediation policy for over-counting (credit same cycle) and under-counting (fix forward).

3) Margin protection
   - If we observe sustained region/hardware COGS inflation that puts burst GM below 50% at the approved floor, we either constrain burst availability/caps or revisit pricing.

4) Rollout discipline
   - No broad GA enablement without SRE sign-off that the non-burst SLO regression gate is functioning (i.e., we can auto-reduce/disable burst when neighbor latency regresses).

Please attach these conditions to the PM pricing ticket and the GA checklist so there’s no ambiguity later.

Laura Bennett
Finance
Redwood Inference


From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 21, 2025 at 9:43 AM PST
Subject: Re: Approval request: Dedicated Burst option pricing bands + margin guardrails (GA target June)

Thanks Laura.

Lauren—please make sure the GA launch brief includes (a) the best-effort language, and (b) the specific billing + SLO gates as launch blockers.

Also, I’d like Sales enablement to have one crisp line: “Burst is for peaks; if you need guaranteed steady-state capacity, increase your reservation.”

Jordan Blake
VP, GTM Operations
Redwood Inference
